notes: Both coders gave delegates for all 4 documents. Policy types almost always agreed; disagreements were mainly actor (admin vs all vs instructor for institutional statements; resolved by who the sentence addresses: all for values/rationale, instructor for instructor-directed guidance), phase (general vs during-work vs when-misuse; resolved by whether the passage is a definition or a rule on doing work), and modality for hedged sentences (informs kept where 'will be' or fact statements, not strengthened). Sample syllabus language on the Instructor Autonomy page was coded by A as rules binding students and by B as options for instructors; resolved as student-addressed rules with document stance delegates and tiers. Unit-level differences: A merged or B split a few sentences (DoS rules vary / Most professors; student guide syllabus vs instructor check). Dropped: A's 'NJIT promotes the use of active learning' (not about AI) and B's 'Unless cited or permitted' (folded into the plagiarism definition unit). Kept after source check: A's equity statement, 'many faculty may encourage or require', student-guide commitment and verify-with-instructor; B's tool list, syllabus-rules sentence, copyright definition, multiple-source comparison, equity goal, check-the-syllabus. B used non-codebook topic labels, replaced by codebook topics. fit_notes added for P35, P54, P10 and P44/P51 loose fits.
